definition: The study of computation in nervous systems using quantitative models, algorithms, and data analysis.
An explicit, simplified representation of variables, relationships, and assumptions.
Generation of state trajectories or synthetic data by applying a model's rules.
Using data to constrain unknown states, parameters, or models.
A model's quantitative output for data not used in fitting, under specified conditions.
The property that some possible observation could conflict with a model's prediction.
A family of methods that optimize predictive functions from data; it overlaps with computational neuroscience but is not identical to it.
The broad practice of organizing, analyzing, computing with, and interpreting data.
A model whose variables and interactions are interpreted as candidate biological processes.
A quantity held fixed during one model run but potentially estimated from data.
A single number; it may be represented as a 1×1 object when the context is stated.
An ordered set of components; this course uses column vectors by default.
A two-dimensional array organized by rows and columns that represents a linear map.
The sum of componentwise products of two vectors with the same dimension.
The matrix produced by multiplying a column vector by a row vector.
Elementwise multiplication of objects with the same shape.
A square matrix that is not invertible and has determinant zero.
The probability assigned to each possible outcome of a discrete random variable.
Probability density per unit interval for a continuous random variable.
The distribution of one variable after summing or integrating over the others.
A distribution renormalized after another event or variable is known.
A function of model parameters that measures their relative support with the observations held fixed.
A distribution over an unknown quantity before observing the current data.
The updated distribution obtained by combining likelihood and prior.
An equation that constrains an unknown function through its derivatives.
A state specified at the starting time that selects one trajectory from a family of solutions.
An exact expression written in terms of known functions.
An approximation to the state at discrete time points.
The timescale over which a first-order exponential process removes about 63% of its initial gap.
A solution whose state no longer changes with time.
Numerical integration by taking a small forward step along the current derivative.
Local error caused by omitting higher-order Taylor terms in a finite-difference approximation.
Whether small perturbations decay during a discrete iteration instead of being amplified.
Equations in which the derivatives of multiple states depend on one another.
A space whose coordinates are all state variables and in which a trajectory is represented.
Electric potential inside the cell minus electric potential outside the cell.
Net random motion driven by a concentration gradient.
The energy qφ of a charged particle in an electric potential.
The voltage at which the net flux of one ion is zero.
The voltage at which current through a channel changes direction; in the simplest case, it equals the equilibrium potential.
The reciprocal of resistance, G=1/R.
Charge stored per unit voltage, Q/V.
The algebraic sum of currents entering and leaving a node is zero.
An abstract model that integrates input, emits a spike at threshold, and resets.
A state driven by input while exponentially relaxing toward a baseline.
The timescale C/G_L of a passive membrane's exponential response.
The value V∞ at which the derivative vanishes under constant input.
The smallest indefinitely sustained constant current that can elicit a spike.
The elapsed time between adjacent spikes.
The minimum interval after a spike during which another spike cannot occur.
The conductance scale when all relevant channels are open.
A gating process in which depolarization increases channel opening.
A process in which sustained depolarization reduces channel availability.
An equation describing how voltage propagates and attenuates through space along a neurite.
A representation that discretizes morphology into electrically coupled compartments.
A mapping from a stimulus or state to a response distribution.
A sequence of discrete spike times.
A visualization of spike times arranged by trial.
An average spike-rate estimate obtained by binning across trials.
Count variance divided by count mean.
A probability model for random event times.
Independence of event counts in nonoverlapping time intervals.
Expected response as a function of a stimulus parameter.
Support for a stimulus or parameter after the response is observed.
The parameter or stimulus estimate that maximizes the likelihood.
Local sensitivity of a probability distribution to a small parameter change.
The joint response pattern of multiple neurons.
An information-theoretic lower bound on the variance of an unbiased estimator under regularity conditions.
Correlation of trial residuals at a fixed stimulus.
Similarity of tuning curves across stimuli.
A matrix containing the variance of each dimension and every pairwise covariance.
Distance normalized by the noise covariance.
Shared noise along the stimulus-signal direction that cannot be removed by averaging a larger population.
A readout that does not use all information available in the encoding distribution.
The difference between an estimator's mean and the true value.
A constraint or prior used to reduce variance or complexity.
A generalized function, or distribution, that samples a function under integration.
An operation that shifts a kernel across the input history, weights it, and sums the result.
The time-dependent response caused by one presynaptic spike.
The connection strength from neuron j→i within a network.
The connection from an external input neuron→recurrent-network neuron.
A state in which large excitatory and inhibitory currents approximately cancel in their means.
Balance generated online by recurrent feedback rather than imposed as moment-by-moment equality.
The leading scaling as N grows, such as O(1) or O(√N).
Spike timing with highly variable ISIs that is approximately Poisson-like.
A function that turns the left side of a first-order linear ODE into a product derivative.
A filter that is zero at negative times and depends only on past input.
The timescale of synaptic-current integration or decay.
The timescale on which a population rate approaches F(I).
A regime in which one variable is much faster than another and can be approximately eliminated.
A nonlinearity mapping input current to steady firing rate.
Zero below threshold and increasing linearly above threshold.
A smooth S-shaped function with lower and upper saturation.
An architecture in which information moves in one direction across layers without a recurrent loop.
A lasting increase in synaptic efficacy.
A lasting decrease in synaptic efficacy.
An empirical rule in which weight change depends on relative pre/post spike timing.
A class of rules in which coordinated activity drives changes in connectivity.
A plasticity rule driven by centered pre- and postsynaptic fluctuations.
The direction associated with the largest covariance eigenvalue.
Global rescaling that maintains an overall activity or weight range.
A Hebbian PCA rule with a local normalization term.
A rule that uses a sliding postsynaptic threshold to control LTP and LTD.
An update determined jointly by presynaptic activity, postsynaptic activity, and a third modulatory or teaching signal.
Learning a predictor from input-target pairs.
Prediction of a discrete label.
Prediction of a continuous target.
The connectivity and computations defining a model.
An objective quantifying disagreement between prediction and target.
The vector of parameter derivatives pointing in the direction of fastest local increase.
The scale of each gradient step.
The linear equation satisfied by a least-squares optimum.
An algorithm for efficiently computing multilayer chain-rule gradients.
The derivative of one computational node's output with respect to its input.
A local or functional relation between a stimulus pattern and a response, not merely a screen location.
A preferential response to a class of stimulus structures.
A broad visual pathway associated with motion- and action-related processing.
A broad visual pathway associated with processing related to object identity.
A cascade of a linear filter, nonlinearity, and Poisson spike-count variability.
A receptive-field organization with opposite signs in the center and periphery.
The rectified response of one filter at every location.
A Gaussian-windowed sinusoid.
Having space and time components that can be written as a product.
A preferential response to one direction of motion.
Inferring a system model from input-output data.
An ideal random stimulus with uncorrelated dimensions or time bins and uniform power.
The collection of stimulus histories preceding all spikes.
The mean of the spike-triggered ensemble.
A matrix organizing stimulus vectors by examples or time bins.
The matrix of second derivatives of loss with respect to parameters.
Having equal curvature or variance in every direction.
Removing covariance correlations to obtain variables near unit covariance.
A stimulus whose dimensions have nonzero covariance.
A stimulus-projection direction on which the response depends.
Analysis of covariance in the spike-triggered ensemble.
The response-sensitive subspace spanned by several stimulus filters.
A family of distributions expressible in a specified canonical statistic-parameter form.
η=Xβ.
The mapping between a conditional mean and η.
A log-link GLM for a count or rate.
A logit-link GLM for a Bernoulli outcome.
The linear effect of past spikes on the current conditional response.
A predictive filter applied to the histories of other units.
A normative principle for optimizing an information representation under resource and noise constraints.
Structure that is predictable from other components and transmitted repeatedly.
The −log probability of an event.
Average surprise or uncertainty.
Residual uncertainty after another variable is given.
The reduction in uncertainty about one variable supplied by another.
An entropy-like quantity for a continuous density that can be negative and depends on units.
The maximum mutual information attainable under input constraints.
Making off-diagonal covariance entries approach zero.
A model of what a system should optimize rather than a direct specification of mechanism.
A change in response or model parameters with stimulus statistics or state.
Signal magnitude or power relative to noise.
Statistics or an operator that do not depend on absolute position.
Sinusoidal cycles per unit distance; the vector also encodes direction.
A conversion between position and frequency representations.
A unified representation of sine/cosine amplitude and phase.
Mean squared amplitude of each frequency component.
Making an output spectrum or covariance approximately flat or identity.
Preserving low frequencies while suppressing high frequencies.
Undersampling that makes a high frequency appear as a lower one.
Several processing stages composed in sequence.
A classical V1 cell type selective for orientation and sensitive to spatial phase.
A classical V1 cell type selective for orientation but more invariant to phase.
Matched filters separated by 90° of phase.
A nonlinear model that squares and sums quadrature-filter outputs.
How well model features predict neural responses.
A reduction in center response when the receptive-field surround is stimulated.
A phase-plane curve on which one state derivative equals zero.
A network whose E subnetwork is unstable alone but stabilized by feedback inhibition.
Control based mainly on a prior model or command rather than current feedback correction.
Online correction of action from sensory or state error.
Sensory feedback about body position or force.
A network with feedback loops among its units.
A population activity pattern associated with an eigenvector of W.
Conversion of the same state between neuronal and modal coordinates.
A mode's decay or integration timescale after feedback.
A state whose derivative is zero.
Whether a small perturbation returns to a fixed point.
A mode that accumulates input without leak.
An eigenmode in which both neurons change in the same direction.
An eigenmode in which the two neurons change in opposite directions.
A state space whose coordinates are the activities of individual neurons.
A state space whose coordinates are dynamical eigenmode amplitudes.
A linear method that orders orthogonal directions by the covariance variance they capture.
A covariance eigenvector together with the score obtained by projecting data onto it.
The component of a vector along a specified basis direction.
An approximation of the original data formed from retained components.
A plot of eigenvalue against component index.
The fraction of the total eigenvalue sum retained by selected components.
A neural circuit that can generate a rhythmic motor pattern without periodic sensory drive.
A neuron that oscillates spontaneously through intrinsic dynamics.
A network oscillator in which two mutually inhibitory units alternate activity.
An eigenvalue that encodes both an exponential envelope and oscillatory phase.
A reduced, conductance-based neuron model with two variables.
The trajectories and nullclines in a two-dimensional state space.
A limit cycle that alternates slow drift with fast jumps.
Removal of inhibition when the active neuron terminates its activity.
A transition in which the inhibited neuron recovers first and escapes inhibition.
A closed periodic orbit that attracts nearby trajectories.
A circuit that converts an eye-velocity command into a persistent eye-position signal.
A continuous family of nearly stable states capable of storing a graded value.
The ability of different parameter combinations to produce similar output or function.
The extent to which data uniquely or sufficiently constrain parameters.
The local curvature matrix of loss with respect to parameters.
A parameter combination to whose variation the loss is highly sensitive.
A parameter combination to whose variation the loss is insensitive.
A set of parameterizations that all explain the data adequately.
Offsetting a change in one parameter with changes in others.
A reaching paradigm from a central location to multiple radial targets.
Variation of the mean response with reach direction.
A low-dimensional hidden variable that explains shared population variability.
A mapping from latent coordinates into high-dimensional activity.
A latent-factor model with a temporal Gaussian-process prior.
A target-dependent population state before movement.
Neural directions that do not change the current readout.
Directions that change muscle or device output.
A system that controls an external device from neural activity.
Online control that includes sensory or device feedback.
This lecture's working definition: a brain state partly decoupled from present input and shaped by past events or future goals.
The ability to retain recently encountered information briefly.
Information retained for use in a current computation.
A sample–delay–test memory task.
Neural activity that remains after the stimulus ends.
A decision model that accumulates noisy evidence to bounds.
Choice or accuracy as a function of stimulus strength.
Reaction time as a function of stimulus strength.
A boundary separating different attractor basins.
A state or set toward which nearby states converge under the dynamics.
Adjustment of stimulus–action associations by outcomes.
A variable marking recent pre/post or action activity for modification by a later reward.
Expected reward used to compute a signal above or below expectation.
Approximate matching of choice proportions to obtained-reward proportions.
Expected discounted future reward from the current state or cue.
A rule that updates cue value using reward-prediction error.
Failure of a new cue to learn because an existing predictor leaves zero error.
Reward plus discounted next value minus current value.
The difference between an actual or updated target and predicted value.
Expected return conditioned on a state–action pair.
A framework that learns a policy or value through interaction and rewards.
A learner that selects actions and updates an internal policy or model.
An environment representation used to predict the future and select an action.
The conditional independence of the future from earlier history given the current state and action.
A mapping from states to action probabilities.
The discounted sum of future rewards.
A recursive self-consistency relation for value.
A model-free, off-policy TD control algorithm.
The tradeoff between gathering new information and selecting the currently best action.
A reinforcement-learning approach that learns or uses an environment model for planning.
A neural or computational process that reinstates or simulates state sequences offline.
The recovery of a stored pattern from a partial or noisy cue.
A group of neurons that are coactive and linked by Hebbian connections.
The set of initial states that converge to the same attractor.
The reconstruction of a complete memory from an incomplete cue.
An update scheme that changes only one unit at each step.
A Lyapunov function for a symmetric binary network.
The normalized dot product between the current state and a stored pattern.
Interference from other stored patterns during retrieval of a target pattern.
A stable state that does not correspond to any single stored pattern.
A regime dominated by many disordered metastable states.
A scale parameter for noise in stochastic updates.
The time-dependent change in a memory's dependence on or representation across brain systems.
Memory for a particular event, including its time, place, and details.
Memory for abstract, generalized knowledge.
The reactivation of experience-related neural sequences during rest or sleep.
A framework that combines fast hippocampal learning with slow cortical learning.
A set of formal roles comprising a generative source, a slow predictor, and a one-shot associative memory.
A process that maps similar experiences onto more distinct memory codes.
A process that recovers a stored episode from a partial cue.
The reconstruction or prediction error measured on stored examples.
The expected prediction error on new samples.
The fitting of sample-specific noise that worsens performance on new data.
A model that controls consolidation according to generalization and predictability.
